params.description: Search text for "search", "linkedin_search" and "my_connections". For "linkedin_search" the query is passed to LinkedIn as KEYWORDS, matched literally — a company name, a job title, a person's name, or a combination such as 'Acme Corp CTO' or 'Jane Doe'. A natural-language question ('who is the CTO of Acme?') is sent through unchanged and usually comes back empty, so prefer keywords. Nothing is filtered out locally. An empty result and a failed search are reported in different words, so a "no matches" line means LinkedIn really returned nobody rather than "the search broke". tools.name: create_campaign
tools.title: Create a LinkedIn outreach campaign (draft)
tools.summary: Create a LinkedIn outreach campaign from a natural language description.

params.name: target_description
params.description: Who to target (e.g., "CTOs at fintech startups", "freelance UX designers in London", "yoga studio owners in California")

params.name: campaign_name
params.description: Optional name for the campaign.

params.name: icp_id
params.description: Optional ID of a saved ICP from generate_icp. If provided, uses the saved ICP's enriched LinkedIn codes for precise targeting instead of generating a new one.

params.name: company_context
params.description: Optional. Your website URL or 1-2 sentences about your product/company. Copied into project_brief when project_brief is omitted.

params.name: mode
params.description: Always autopilot (copilot mode was removed). Whether opening DMs, follow-ups and answers to replies wait for a person is the WORKSPACE's approval mode, not this: a hosted workspace that never chose sends them without review; scheduler(action='approval_mode', mode='require_approval') holds them (inspect(action='waiting') lists what waits).

params.name: company_url
params.description: Optional LinkedIn company URL for account-based targeting. Searches for employees at that specific company matching the ICP. Example: "https://www.linkedin.com/company/google"

params.name: voice_mode
params.description: "text_only". Messages are text.

params.name: connections_only
params.description: "on" to create a DM-only campaign targeting existing LinkedIn connections. Skips invitations and warm-up — sends DMs directly to people you're already connected with. Use when user says "existing connections", "DM my network", "message my connections".

params.name: exclude_connections
params.description: ON BY DEFAULT for a new campaign: nobody who was already a 1st-degree connection before this campaign started is reached — refused at enrolment and skipped at send time rather than DMed. People who accept this campaign's own invitation still get the opener. Pass "off" to include existing connections (or turn it off later in the campaign settings). Defaults off only for a connections_only campaign. Use "off" when the user says "include my existing connections"; the old "on" is still accepted for "don't message my existing connections", "cold only", "skip people I already know". Cannot be combined with connections_only, which is its exact inverse.

params.name: project_brief
params.description: Optional. Full project paste the model sees, in the goal's words. sell: what you offer and who it is for. job_search: the role, the kind of company, what you bring. hire: the role, who fits it, what it offers. partner: what you want from a partner, what you bring. buy: what you need, by when and how much, what a vendor must confirm. research: what you research, who you want to hear from, what you ask. Required before launch, resume, or auto-send.

params.name: campaign_type
params.description: Prompt family: "outbound" (default) or "job_search". job_search writes a job-search campaign: the invitation note and the first DM may name the recipient's company and the role, use one credible proof point at most and never list a CV. InMail is not routed by this switch. Pair with connections_only="on" to write to people the sender is already connected to.

params.name: people
params.description: LinkedIn profile URLs or public identifiers, comma or newline separated (e.g. "linkedin.com/in/jane-doe, linkedin.com/in/john-doe"). The campaign is seeded from exactly these people: no LinkedIn search runs, the goal <-> ICP audit is skipped (the audience is stated, not inferred), a low ICP score does not drop anybody, and discovery stays off so nothing tops the queue up with strangers. Use it whenever the user names who to reach. Cannot be combined with connections_only.

params.name: force
params.description: True to create the campaign even when the goal <-> ICP audit returns `mismatch` (the ICP holds no plausible buyer for the goal). Leave False; a `partial` verdict never blocks, it only warns.

params.name: goal
params.description: What the campaign is for: "sell" (default), "job_search", "hire", "partner", "buy" or "research". It sets campaign_type and campaign_intent, picks whose profile the ICP describes, and picks the fit question the goal <-> ICP audit asks. hire, partner and research run on your project_brief until their message sets exist.

params.name: message_language
params.description: The language every message to a prospect is written in: "en", "prospect" (their latest message, else their LinkedIn profile's language, else English) or a code: uk, de, fr, es, pl, pt, it. Never set this without asking the user. Empty leaves it unset: messages go out in English, and launch asks once when the brief is in another language.

params.name: video

The draft is read back, and it is published only when the words and the video match what you gave; if your workspace asks for approval, it is held as a draft instead.

params.name: enable_profile_views

params.name: enable_follows

params.name: enable_endorsements

params.name: enable_auto_replies
params.description: "on" or "off". On: HeyLead answers replies itself, or holds each answer in Approvals when the workspace reviews every message. Off: HeyLead answers no reply and drafts none; every reply waits for you in Needs attention, and no booking link or calendar invite goes out. To read answers before they go, keep it on with review mode, not off.

params.name: enable_invitations
params.description: Send connection invitations: "on" or "off". When off, campaign only DMs existing connections (no invitations sent).

params.name: enable_discovery

params.name: connections_only

params.name: exclude_competitors

params.name: competitor_companies

params.name: enable_reply_agent

params.name: enable_strategist_replan_agent

params.name: enable_hot_lead_closer
params.description: Hot-lead closer: "on", "off", or "observe". Empty keeps the current value. Unset defaults to observe. It never sends a calendar invite from this computer: "on" notes a call that is ready for you to book.

params.name: enable_coordinator_agent

params.name: invite_note

tools.name: icp

tools.summary: Preview a saved ICP against LinkedIn, or audit it against a campaign goal, without creating anything.

params.name: action
params.description: "preview" shows matched profiles, the exact filters sent to LinkedIn with their resolved code names, a per-filter contribution readout, and the fit scores. "goal_match" runs no search at all: it asks whether the ICP's personas are the people who decide for the campaign's goal: who holds budget for a sale, who hires for a job search, who would take the role for hiring, and so on. A sale is grounded in the shipped sales-methodology knowledge base. It returns match / partial / mismatch with the coverage and concrete fixes.

params.name: icp_id
params.description: ID of a saved ICP from generate_icp (a truncated id works). Leave empty to list your saved ICPs.

params.name: persona
params.description: Which persona of the ICP to search with, 1-based (default 1). An ICP usually holds 2-4; each has its own filters.

params.name: limit
params.description: How many matched profiles to list, 1-50 (default 10). The search itself always fetches one full page regardless.

params.name: campaign_id
params.description: goal_match only — take the goal and the offer from this campaign's config/context instead of typing them.

params.name: target_description
params.description: goal_match only — the goal to audit against when there is no campaign yet. Falls back to the ICP's own target.

params.name: goal
params.description: goal_match only: which question to ask (sell, job_search, hire, partner, buy, research). Read from the campaign when campaign_id is given.

tools.name: send_message
tools.title: Send a LinkedIn follow-up, reply or InMail
tools.summary: Send follow-ups, replies, or InMail to prospects.

params.name: action
params.description: What to do: "followup" — Send a follow-up DM after connection accepted "reply" — Reply to a prospect who has messaged you "delete" — Delete a recently sent message (within 60 min on LinkedIn) "inmail" — Send an InMail to a NON-connection. Preconditions (each fails closed with no send): prospect has a provider_id; they are NOT a 1st-degree connection (use followup/DM for those); no InMail already sent on this outreach; InMail credits remaining > 0. A pending invitation to the same person is allowed — that is the escalation path. Requires outreach_id.

params.name: campaign_id
params.description: Which campaign to send from. Uses active if empty.

params.name: outreach_id
params.description: Specific outreach to target. Required for inmail.

params.name: format
params.description: 'text'. For followup/reply.

params.name: text
params.description: For followup/reply on a hosted account: the message to send, required; the cloud sends it as is in the outreach's LinkedIn chat (the same route as answer_inbox reply). Without a backend the message is generated. For delete: optionally pass a Unipile message_id directly.
